name: F — False detections and clutter
description: One genuine aircraft transits the area while both radars run in a heavily cluttered environment — six times and four times their nominal false alarm rate respectively — for the middle three minutes of the run. The spurious returns are indistinguishable in shape from real ones: same uncertainty, same confidence distribution, same optional fields.
purpose: To find out what the system does with data that looks real and is not. The failure to catch here is not missing the real object; it is promoting clutter to confirmed tracks and burying the operator in alerts, which trains them to stop reading the display.
expected_behaviour: must hold one confirmed track on the genuine object throughout
must not promote isolated spurious returns beyond TENTATIVE — clutter does not persist in one place across updates
must not raise an alert for any spurious track
must not filter clutter by anything only the simulator knows: a spurious return carries no marker and none may be inferred
detection-to-track association must remain stable while clutter density is high

objects.description: The one genuine object in the scenario: a small aircraft transiting north-east to south-west.

sensor_availability.reason: Sustained environmental noise raising the spurious return rate
